metadata.title: Micron's 19% Rally Sends AI Chip Stocks Surging

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Semiconductor stocks are pushing higher in early trading as Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) gave investors another reason to believe the AI chip cycle could still have more room to run. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF rose 5% in US premarket trading, while Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) jumped 12%, Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) climbed 12%, and Seagate Technology (NASDAQ:STX) added 8.3%, showing how quickly confidence returned across the memory and storage space.
Micron, the largest US maker of computer memory chips, rallied 19% after results came in ahead of Wall Street expectations. The company said revenue could reach approximately $50 billion in its fiscal fourth quarter through August, well above analysts' average estimate of $43.2 billion. Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) also strengthened the AI narrative, gaining 13% in early Thursday trading after forecasting more than $15 billion a year in sales by fiscal 2029 from AI components for data centers.
The move spread across the broader chip sector, with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) rising 1.2%, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) gaining 3.8%, and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) adding 6.2%. The rally extends what has already been a historic run, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index up 90% so far in 2026 and possibly on pace for its strongest annual gain since 1999. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said there was no line of sight to when supply could catch up with demand, while Citigroup analyst Atif Malik wrote that demand for high bandwidth memory products remains far above Micron's available supply.
